 Judgment
The petitioners have filed this petition U/Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1988 claiming compensation amount
from respondents due to death of Sri. Ravindra M. in a road traffic accident.
2. Brief case of the petit

ioners is that, on 28-10-2023 at about 1.30 p.m. the deceased Ravindra M.
was walking on the extreme side foot path of MES Service Road, i.e., from BEL Circle and proceeding towards Kuvempu Circle, Jalahalli, Bangalore and reached near Kuvempu Circle, at that time all of a sudden a Goods Carriage vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-39/T-3618 driven by its driver at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endangering to human life and came on wrong lane and lost control over his vehicle and dashed against the deceased from behind and caused the accident.

Due to forced impact, deceased fell down and subsequently, the front wheel of Jyothi .G vs National Ins Co Ltd on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182575125/
2 the said Goods Carriage ran over his head.

sentences.text:
Due to the tremendous impact, the deceased Ravindra M.
succumbed to the fatal injuries on the spot.
3. Later on the postmortem was done in the M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bangalore.

The said accident is a severe tragedy to the petitioners family and they have to suffer irreparable loss, damage untold misery due to the said accident and they have spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards the death,
funeral and obsequies ceremonies and also towards transportation of dead body.

4. Prior to the date of accident deceased was hale, healthy and aged about 40 years and working as self employed and also working at Acharya College, Bangalore and earning a sum of Rs.45,000/-p.m. and Rs.300/- bata per day.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased and she has lost her husband's love and affection, caring at early age due to the fatal accident.
Petitioner No.2 to 4 are children of the deceased and now they have to grow without love and affection and guidelines of the father.
The petitioner No.5 and 6 are the parents of the deceased and they have lost their son at their old age.
The petitioners were entirely depending upon the deceased.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the family members are having lot of pain, shock, mental agony and financial difficulties.

5. The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Goods Carriage vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-39/T-3618, against whom the Jalahalli Traffic Police filed criminal case in Cr.No.258/2023 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC r/w Sec.134(a & b) and 187 of M.V. Act.
6. Respondent No.1 is being Insurer and respondent No.2 being RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners pray to grant the compensation.
7. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsel and filed their separate objection to the main petition.
8. Respondent No.1 has contended that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law and facts, the same is liable to be dismissed in limine.
Further, it is admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-39/T-3618.

Further, it has contended that, the said vehicle and its driver has been implicated in the alleged accident by the petitioners and jurisdictional police and respondent No.2 have also co-operated with the petitioner in doing the same.
The complaint has been registered against the unknown vehicle, but, the jurisdictional police have seized the vehicle and filed false charge sheet against the driver of respondent No.2
, without conducting proper investigation this vehicle has been implicated in the alleged accident for illegal gain.

Further, it is contended that, the alleged accident was took place only due to careless and negligence act on the part of the deceased, who was crossing the road in a careless manner, without observing moving vehicles and at that time unknown vehicle caused the alleged accident and ran over from the spot.

Further, contended that, the alleged driver of respondent No.2 vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. and without FC and permit plied the vehicle and thereby respondent No.2 has violated the policy conditions.
Further denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased.

It is contended Jyothi .G vs National Ins Co Ltd on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182575125/
3 that, the compensation amount claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated, arbitrary and speculative.

9. Respondent No.2 has contended in his objection to main petition that, the petition filed by the petitioners is frivolous and vexatious and it has been filed with oblique motive and to harass him and to have unlawful gain.
It is further contended that, he is the owner of the Goods Carriage Vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-39/T-3618, it has valid policy issued by respondent No.1 and vehicle had the fitness certificate.
Further, he has contended that, at the time of accident it was driven by his driver and he was driving the vehicle carefully, therefore, he is not liable to pay the compensation.

Further, it is contended that, the compensation amount claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated,
arbitrary and speculative.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

10. Based on the above pleadings, this Tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, on 28-10- 2023 at about 1.30 p.m. the deceased Ravindra M. was walking on footpath of MES Service Road,
near Kuvempu Circle, Jalahalli, Bangalore wherein the driver of Goods Carriage Vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-39/T-3618 drove it with speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased from behind and caused the accident, due to which, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot?
2) Whether the respondent No.1 proves that insured has violated the policy conditions as contended at para 20 of written statement?
3) Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so how much?

From whom?
4) Whether order or award?
11.
In order to prove the case, petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 21 documents marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.21.
The petitioners got examined the eyewitness by name Prajwal Sriramulu Barigidad as PW.2 and got marked a document as Ex.P.22.
Further, the petitioners got examined the I.O.'s as PW.3 and PW.4 and got marked documents as Ex.P.23 to P.27.

Per contra, Respondent No.1 got examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1 and 2.
12.
Heard the arguments on the side of the petitioner.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and 2 have filed written arguments along with citations.
Perused the materials available on record.

13. By considering the evidence and arguments, this court answer the following issues as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.

REASONS 14. Issue Nos.1 & 2:- These issues are taken together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts.

The petitioners have filed this petition against respondents for claiming compensation from the respondents, due to death of husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioner No.2 to 4 and son of petitioner No.5 and 6 in a road traffic accident.

15. In order to substantiate the case, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief- examination and in her chief affidavit, she had reiterated the entire contention of petition and got marked 21 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.21.

16 . Ex.P.1 is the copy of F.I.R, Ex.P.2 is the copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot Sketch,
Ex.P.4 is the copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the copy of Inquest Report, Ex.P.6 is the copy of vehicle seizure mahazar, Ex.P.7 is the copy of IMV Report, Ex.P.8 is the copy of PM Report, Ex.P.9 is the copy of statement of driver, Ex.P.10 is the copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act, Ex.P.11 is the copy of reply to the Notice, Ex.P.12 is the Indeminity Bond, Ex.P.13 is the final report, Ex.P.14 is the copy of Aadhar Card of the deceased and Ex.P.15 is the copy of D.L.
Ex.P.16 to 21 are the copies of Aadhar Cards of the petitioners.
In the cross-examination she has stated that, she has given statement before the police, she was informed about the vehicle, after verifying the CCTV Footage.
On the same day, the CCTV Footage and vehicle has been shown to her.
Police have shown the vehicle after seizure, there was scratches on the right side of the vehicle.
Further, she denied that the vehicle is not involved in the accident.
17. The petitioners got examined the eyewitness by name Prajwal Sriramulu Barigidad as PW.2 and got marked a document as Ex.P.22, which is the copy of Aadhar Card of PW.2.

In the chief-examination he has stated that, on 28- 10-2023 at about 1.30 p.m. he was proceeding on his motorcycle at BEL Circle Road, at that time the Lorry No.AP-39/T-3618 came on wrong lane in a rash & negligent manner and dashed to the pedestrian from behind.
He parked his motorcycle nearby and rushed to the spot.
The driver of the Lorry stopped his vehicle looked back at the spot and ran away along with the vehicle.
He has given statement before the Police.
In cross-examination he has stated that, he was going to his friends house, it was Saturday.
On Monday he has stated the vehicle number to the police.
18. Further the petitioners got examined the I.O. of this case as PW.3 and got marked 05 documents as Ex.P.23 to P.27.
Ex.P.23 is the copy of Letter for Assignment, Ex.P.24 is the copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act, Ex.P.25 and 26 are the Photos of the Lorry, Ex.P.27 is the C.D.

In the chief-examination he has stated that, PSI has assigned him to trace out the vehicle, one eye-witness Jyothi .G vs National Ins Co Ltd on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182575125/

24. RW.1 has deposed that, the vehicle is not involved in the accident, it has been falsely implicated in the accident.
On perusal of the objection of respondent No.1/owner it appears that, he has not denied the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Respondent No.1 in his objection has clearly admitted that, at the time of accident his driver was driving the vehicle.
25. Further, PW.1 has stated about the involvement of the vehicle and tracing the Lorry on the basis CCTV Footage.
PW.2 the eye-witness of the incident has clearly spoke about the witnessing the incident and identifying of the Lorry and Driver.
PW.3 and 4 the IO's of this case have stated about the tracing of the vehicle through eye-witness and CCTV Footage.
On perusal of evidence of PW.1 to 4, it is clear that, the Lorry bearing its No.AP-39/T-3618 has caused and involved in the said accident.

Therefore, it appears that this accident is caused by the Lorry bearing its No.AP-39/T-3618.
26.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Allahabad 2011 ACJ 1261 in between Oriental Insurance Co Ltd. Vs. Reena Awasthi & Others,
wherein it is held that, the number of the motorcycle was not disclosed in FIR, but it was detected during the investigation.

sentences.text: Independent witness stated that the motorcycle driven rashly and negligently and caused the accident.
The findings of the Tribunal based on the independent witness has been upheld by the Hon'ble High Court.
Therefore, on perusal of the said judgment it appears that, the deposition of the independent witness if doesn't seem to suffer from any personal interest can be believed.
The tribunal can rely upon the statement of the independent witness.

Further relied upon a judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in 2011 ACJ 552 in between Saroj and others Vs. Het Lal and others, wherein the said judgment the owner/respondent No.2 has admitted the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.

Therefore, on the basis of the ratio laid down in the above judgment, as the owner/respondent No.2 of this case has admitted the involvement of the vehicle in the accident is sufficient to hold that, the vehicle is involved in the accident.

27. Further, the petitioner relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in 2013 AIR SCW 5375 in between Minu Rout and Another Vs. sentences.text: Tribunal must rely upon the evidence lead before it.
On perusal of the ratio laid down in the said judgment, it is clear that the Tribunal ought to have relied upon the evidence lead before it and not the charge sheet.
This Tribunal has considered the oral evidence lead by the petitioners and other supporting documents produced by the petitioners and not solely relied upon the charge sheet.
In the said judgment, as per the case the deceased was travelling in the Truck but, in evidence of claimants stated that, the deceased was a pedestrian.
The facts of the said case are quite different to the case on hand.
Hence, the judgment relied by respondent No.1 is not helpful to its defence.

29. Further relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2000 KAR 1817 in between Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation Vs. Smt. Laxmibai, wherein it is held that, the accident has to prove by sufficient and cogent evidence.

But, in the present case, the petitioners have produced sufficient evidence as discussed above.
Hence, the judgment relied by respondent No.1 is not helpful to its case.
30. On perusal of Ex.P.3 the sketch, it appears that the accident had occurred at the right portion of the road i.e., ahead in the middle portion of the road.

The deceased was walking on the extreme side footpath of MES Service Road, i.e., from BEL Circle and proceeding towards Kuvempu Circle,
Jalahalli, Bangalore.
There was enough space on the left side of the road to avoid the accident by the driver of offending vehicle.

On perusal of Spot sketch & Charge sheet which disclose that, when the deceased was walking at the extreme side of the road, the driver of the offending vehicle, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased and caused the accident.
Hence, the Jalahalli Traffic Police have filed Charge sheet against driver of offending vehicle as accused for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC r/w Sec.134(a & b), 187 of IMV Act.
Therefore, it is clear that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

31. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 Jyothi .G vs National Ins Co Ltd on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182575125/
8 the petitioners have to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.

sentences.text: 32. The respondent No.1 has taken contention that the respondent No.2 has violated the policy terms and conditions, but the respondent No.1 has not produced oral or documentary evidence to prove its contention.
There is nothing on record to show that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, this Court is of considered opinion that the respondent No.1 has not proved that respondent No.2 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

33. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1-F.I.R, Ex.P.2- Complaint, Ex.P.3-Spot Sketch, Ex.P.4-Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.5-Inquest Report, Ex.P.6-Vehicle Seizure Mahazar, Ex.P.7-IMV Report, Ex.P.8-PM Report, Ex.P.9-Statement of Driver, Ex.P.10-Notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act, Ex.P.11-Reply to the Notice and Ex.P.13-Charge sheet, it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Good Carriage Vehicle bearing Reg.No.AP-39/ T-3618.
Hence, this Tribunal answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative and Issue No.2 in the Negative.
34. Issue No.3: The petitioners claimed compensation amount of Rs.80,00,000/- with respect to death of husband of petitioner No.1 Sri. Ravindra M. in a road traffic accident.
35. As per Ex.P.14 Notarized Copy of Aadhaar Card, date of birth of the deceased is shown as 06-04-1983.
As per Ex.P.5 Inquest Report and Ex.P.8 PM Report also age of the deceased is shown as 40 years.
On the basis of the date of birth of the deceased in the Aadhar Card, he was of 40 years old.
Hence, the age of the deceased is taken in between 36 to 40 at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier is 15.
36.
The petitioners not produced any documents to prove the income and avocation of the deceased.
In present days a Coolie worker can get Rs.400/- to 500/- per day.

However, the petitioners asserted that the deceased was working as self employed and also working at Acharya College,
Bangalore and earning a sum of Rs.45,000/-p.m. though documents are not produced but, by considering the age, income and occupation of deceased this Tribunal took the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.16,000/-.
37.

With regard to the loss of future prospectus is concern, the Apex court in the earlier Judgment reported in 2013 ACJ 1403 (Rajesh & Ors Vs Rajbir Singh & Ors) also taken note of the fact that, self employed persons are also entitled for future prospectus and the said Judgment was referred to larger bench and the Apex court in the recent Judgment passed in 2017 ACJ 2700 SC (between National Insurance co. ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others.)

An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the income minus the tax component"
